goldens.comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.
goldens.reasoning: C1 describes the same issue as G1's second part: in the noscript header, .panel sits inside .row and isn't a flex item, so it loses its right alignment.

goldens.comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
-webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
goldens.reasoning: C2 raises the same problem: the ordinal-group properties are 1-based, so passing $val straight through gives the wrong order.

candidates: No-ember header right-align broken: The PR changes .panel alignment to rely on flexbox (margin-left:auto/order), but the Rails fallback header wraps .panel inside a Bootstrap v2 .row which is float-based (not a flex container). Therefore .panel is not a flex item in that path and will no longer right-align on noscript and /no_ember pages.

order mixin ordinal-group off-by-one: The order mixin passes $val directly to -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group, but the old flexbox spec uses 1-based indexing (default: 1) while the standard order property is 0-based (default: 0). This causes incorrect element ordering in older browsers.
